abstract: Transplantable mouse teratomas are known to contain multipotential teratocarcinoma stem cells analogous to early embryo cells and capable of giving rise to a wide variety of specialized cell types in vivo when they attach to a substratum; if they are grown instead in suspension in the body cavity, they form multicellular embryoid bodies which proliferate with little or no cell specialization. Thus, changes initiated at the cell surface may play some role in promoting early cell differentiation. In order to establish an in vitro system for experimental investigation of this hypothesis, embryoid body cells were explanted under conditions of cell attachment versus suspension and maintained in primary culture. Because cell differentiation in previous reports was relatively limited in vitro, the two cellular populations were first compared for genesis of a quantifiable macromolecular phenotype, acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity, which characterizes several of the cell types most commonly formed in the attached tumors in vivo. The attached cells produced markedly increased levels of AChE activity within a few weeks, while cells in suspension retained basal levels. AChE was histochemically visualized and was found to occur chiefly in cells undergoing myogenesis, especially during myotube formation. Aberrant muscle fibers formed and became predominant in the cultures. When embryoid bodies were first fractionated by increasing size, which reflects their progressive differentiation, the smallest ones, with relatively more multipotential cells and no apparent muscle cells, also showed AChE increase in attached cultures. The results are consistent with the view that attachment of the cell surface to a substratum may play a critical role in initiating some cellular developmental commitments, as well as in sustaining differentiation of cells whose specialization has already been determined. Further experimental modifications of this primary culture system of teratocarcinoma cells should be useful in analyzing cell-substratum relations and cell-surface changes in early mammalian development.
abstract_ja: マウスの奇形腫は、多能性の奇形癌幹細胞を含むことが知られており、これは培養された胚と類似し、基質に付着すると、体内で多様な特殊化した細胞型を生じることができる。一方、浮遊状態で体腔内で培養すると、細胞の特殊化をほとんど伴わず増殖する胚様体を形成する。したがって、細胞表面に起こる変化が初期の細胞分化の促進に何らかの役割を果たしている可能性がある。この仮説を実験的に検討するための体外系を確立するため、胚様体細胞を付着条件と浮遊条件で外植し、初代培養で維持した。以前の報告では体外での細胞分化が比較的限られていたため、まず両集団を、生体内で付着腫瘍に最も多く形成される細胞型の1つであるアセチルコリンエステラーゼ(AChE)活性という定量可能な高分子表現型の生成について比較した。付着細胞では数週間以内にAChE活性が著明に増加し、浮遊細胞では基礎レベルにとどまった。AChEは組織化学的に可視化され、主に筋形成、特に筋管形成の過程にある細胞に認められた。異常な筋線維が形成され、培養中で優勢となった。サイズごとに分画された胚様体は、サイズが大きいほど分化が進んでいることを反映しており、最も小さいもの、すなわち多能性細胞がより多く、筋細胞がほとんど見られないものでも、付着培養ではAChE活性の増加を示した。これらの結果は、細胞表面が基質に付着することが、細胞の発生的な決定の開始や、既に特殊化が決まった細胞の分化の維持に重要な役割を果たしうるという見解と一致する。この奇形癌細胞の初代培養系をさらに実験的に改変することは、哺乳類の初期発生における細胞と基質の関係や細胞表面の変化を解析するうえで有用であろう。
